Caveat: the evidence is operator interviews with a small sample, and the legal structure must be validated state by state.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick two states with well-documented qualifier rules (for example FL and TX) and pay for a counsel memo on each. Recruit 10 retired license holders through trade associations, retiree groups and union alumni networks. Build a one-page lender-facing continuity plan and show it to 10-15 SBA lenders and 20 business brokers. Post the offer in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience) and sign 2-3 buyers with signed LOIs for paid pilot placements at a discount in exchange for case studies.

ideas.title: Orphaned Job and Membership Rescue Desk
ideas.one_liner: When a PE roll-up of contractors collapses, package its unfinished jobs, prepaid maintenance memberships and warranties and hand them to healthy local contractors, while lenders and trustees get paid for the recovery.
ideas.customer: Two payers. (1) Private-credit lenders, Chapter 11 trustees and creditor committees of collapsed home-service platforms, on a success fee. (2) Local independent contractors and newly formed tech-owned shops, who pay a per-customer transfer fee to inherit service obligations and customer relationships.
ideas.problem: Roll-ups of HVAC, remodeling and roofing firms are failing, and the stranded parties have no one to coordinate. Homeowners are left with half-finished jobs and prepaid plans. Laid-off technicians hold the customer relationships but not the customer data. Lenders are owed $100M+ from shells with almost no assets and have no operating capability to finish jobs and collect receivables.
ideas.solution: A rapid-response playbook plus lightweight software: (1) an intake site for stranded customers ('my contractor shut down'); (2) an import of the estate's job, warranty and membership data from its field-service or CRM exports, scored by job stage, deposit status, and geography; (3) matching to vetted local contractors, with milestone escrow so the deposit follows the work; (4) a lender/trustee dashboard showing completed WIP and recovered receivables. A starter kit (entity formation, insurance, licensing checklist, FSM software setup) lets laid-off technicians become buyers of the books they used to serve.
ideas.why_now: 2025 was a record year for PE-linked distress. The PE Stakeholder Project counts PE firms in 19 of the 35 largest US bankruptcies (54%) and 21 of 41 large ones (51%) in 2025, though it is an advocacy source. Bain's 2026 reports say borrowing costs are 8-9% versus 6-7% a decade ago, and deals now need 10-12% annual EBITDA growth to hit target returns. That squeezes leveraged service roll-ups. Private credit, not banks, now holds much of the paper, and these lenders lack turnaround operations for field-service businesses.
ideas.revenue_model: 5-10% success fee on WIP completed and receivables recovered for the estate. $150-400 per customer transferred, paid by the acquiring contractor. Optional 1-1.5% escrow fee on consumer deposits. Subscription for lenders who want a watchlist and pre-built playbook.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: In a roll-up collapse the valuable asset is the unfulfilled service obligations (prepaid memberships, warranties, half-built jobs), not the brand or customer list. Local independents will pay to inherit them, and lenders recover more from orderly completion than from a liquidation. Renovo, formed in 2021 by Audax by combining three home-remodeling businesses (later seven), filed in November 2025 with about $50,000 in assets against more than $100M in liabilities, after roughly $150M from BlackRock, Apollo and Oaktree. About 1,500 workers were terminated, some without final paychecks, and homeowners were left with incomplete projects. Cutting installer pay from 10-12% to 8% drove out skilled workers (https://pestakeholder.org/private-equity-bankruptcy-tracker/). In September 2026 PE-backed United Air Temp (Littlejohn's United Comfort Group, eight partner companies) filed WARN notices for 135+ layoffs across VA and MD, closing its Lorton HQ effective Nov 10, 2026 (https://www.achrnews.com/articles/166687-private-equity-backed-united-air-temp-announces-mass-layoffs). WARN notices are a free, public lead source for the next rescue.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a watchlist from public WARN notices and bankruptcy dockets for home-service platforms. Stand up a 'my contractor shut down' landing page and intake form for one distressed metro. Sign 5 local independent contractors who agree to take transferred customers at a flat fee. Cold-approach restructuring counsel and Chapter 11 trustees at 5-10 private-credit special-situations desks with a free 2-week pilot on a small estate. Estate authority over customer data will be the gating legal step, so line up a bankruptcy attorney early.

ideas.title: Seller-Brain Capture and Margin Leak Audit
ideas.one_liner: In the 90-day handover, reverse-engineer the retiring owner's pricing and rules of thumb from years of quotes and invoices, and find the contract and price leaks the seller never fixed, for a fee tied to recovered margin.
ideas.customer: First-time acquirers (search funders, independent sponsors, SBA-financed buyers, small holdcos) of $1-15M revenue service and light-manufacturing firms. SBA lenders and brokers are secondary referrers.
ideas.problem: The seller's pricing logic lives in his head, records are paper or Excel, and the handover is a 'handshake and good luck'. New owners find contractual minimums unbilled, price books frozen for years, parts sold below cost, and waste in telecom and software. They discover this only after closing, when the seller is already leaving.
ideas.solution: A 30-day sprint at signing or close. (1) Ingest 3 years of quotes, invoices, price books, contracts and vendor, phone and SaaS bills, including scanned paper. (2) An AI model reconstructs the implicit pricing rules and flags exceptions. (3) A structured, recorded 3-hour seller interview validates and labels the rules. (4) Output a working quote calculator, a written 'rules of thumb' manual, and a ranked leak list in dollars (unbilled contractual minimums, stale prices vs inflation, below-cost jobs and parts, dead subscriptions). The seller reviews the model weekly during the transition period.
ideas.why_now: Bain's 2026 reports say deals now need 10-12% EBITDA growth to hit returns and 79% of GPs expect flat purchase multiples, so operational upside has to be found rather than bought. Buyers of small firms feel the same pressure. LLMs now read messy PDFs, scans and Excel cheaply, which makes a 10-day audit cost a few hundred dollars in compute instead of a consultant's month.
ideas.revenue_model: $4-6K fixed fee for the capture sprint, plus 10-15% of annualized recovered margin in year one (capped). Optional pre-LOI 'upside memo' at $1.5-2.5K that buyers use to justify a bid and negotiate price.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The leaks are contractual and forgotten, not strategic, and the seller's pricing logic is a perishable asset that expires with the transition period. Concrete cases from ETA operators: Tew & Taylor's contracts specified a two-hour minimum but the prior owner billed one hour, and after the buyer applied the contract rate there was 'virtually no customer pushback' (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/jack-rauch-tew-taylor). At Cardinal Heating & Air, prices were unchanged since pre-COVID, parts were sold below cost, and the buyer cut $1.4M of annualized cost in two weeks ($10K/month in cell phones vs $3K needed). Gross margins went from 7-20% to 48-49% (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/mike-bourgeois-cardinal-heating-and-air). At Winsor Fireform, pricing was the seller's 27 years of 'hunches', and the buyers 'sprinted' to extract it into a model during his 3-month transition; gross margin rose from 55% to 58-59% (https://acquiringminds.co/articles/andrew-sova-alex-clark-winsor-fireform-novo-foundry). At Gary Air, prices had not kept pace with inflation for 4+ years, and earnings went from $340K SDE to $1.3M EBITDA in 14 months (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air). Four independent buyers found the same class of leak and each rebuilt it by hand.
ideas.first_30_days: Offer free audits to 10 first-time buyers found in ETA communities (Searchfunder, Acquiring Minds audience, ETA subreddits) in exchange for permission to publish anonymized before/after numbers. Build parsers for QuickBooks exports and for invoice exports from ServiceTitan, Jobber and Housecall Pro, plus a vendor-bill classifier. Create a one-page seller-interview protocol. Convert the first 3 free audits into case studies, then switch to contingency pricing.

ideas.title: Liquidity for Managers of Overheld PE Companies
ideas.one_liner: Give executives in stuck PE portfolio companies a way to cash out part of their vested equity through third-party buyers, so sponsors can fix management retention without diluting the fund or forcing an exit.
ideas.customer: Lower-middle-market PE sponsors and independent sponsors holding 2019-2021 vintage platforms. They pay for the diagnostic. Portfolio-company CEOs, CFOs and operators hold vested profits interests or options. Family offices and secondary funds supply the capital that buys management equity.
ideas.problem: Hold periods have stretched to roughly seven years. Management teams are fatigued and their incentive plans have lost value, which raises the risk they leave. The fund cannot exit (LPs tolerate little markdown), and topping up the management incentive plan (MIP) dilutes the sponsor's remaining upside.
ideas.solution: (1) A 'MIP Health Check': a waterfall model built from the operating agreement showing each manager's equity value under three exit dates and prices, with a retention-risk score. (2) A 'management tender desk': arrange third-party purchase of 10-25% of a manager's vested units at a negotiated discount, with sponsor consent and rights of first refusal, funded by a syndicate of family offices and secondary funds. (3) A cost and dilution comparison against a traditional MIP reload. Structured through a registered broker-dealer partner and securities counsel.
ideas.why_now: Bain's 2026 midyear report says most buyout assets were acquired in 2021 or earlier, the implied capital cycle is about seven years, and roughly one in five LPs are cutting buyout allocations. Bain's year-end outlook counts 32,000 unrealized companies worth $3.8T and says 40% of portfolio companies are held over 5 years, versus 29% in 2019. Fund-level returns flatten after year eight, so the pressure to retain operators through the extended hold is acute.
ideas.revenue_model: $5-10K per MIP Health Check billed to the sponsor. 1.5-3% placement fee on tender volume, paid by buyers. Later, SaaS for waterfall tracking at $1-3K/month per fund.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is human capital inside assets that cannot be sold, and the only retention lever that costs the fund nothing in dilution is third-party liquidity for managers. Bain's midyear report says: 'Stretched holding periods have fatigued management teams and depleted incentive plan value, complicating mid-hold value-creation refreshes,' and that more than half of LPs cap tolerated markdowns on full exits at 5%, which pushes GPs to hold underperformers longer (https://www.bain.com/insights/private-equity-midyear-report-2026/). 'Stretched holds' and '12 is the new 5' EBITDA growth targets (https://www.bain.com/insights/welcome-to-a-new-era-global-private-equity-report-2026/) mean operators are being asked to deliver more for longer. Employee tender offers are routine in venture-backed startups but are, by my inference, rare for PE-backed profits interests, so this looks like an open niche. That is an inference from the sources, not something they state. Regulatory structure is the main risk.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a profits-interest waterfall calculator from a standard operating-agreement template. Retain securities and tax counsel for a scoping memo and line up a registered broker-dealer partner. Offer free Health Checks to 15 independent sponsors and lower-mid-market GPs with 2019-2021 vintage assets, reached through ACG, Searchfunder and direct outreach. Then sign 2-3 paid checks at $5K and use the results to pitch one family office to fund a first tender.

ideas.title: File-Cabinet-to-Pipeline Digitization Crew
ideas.one_liner: A mobile scan-and-extract crew that turns a newly acquired trades company's filing cabinets and paper job files into a clean customer and equipment-age database plus a ready-to-run replacement and membership campaign.
ideas.customer: Acquirers of legacy HVAC, plumbing, roofing, pest, electrical and garage-door companies (search funders, holdcos, PE add-on platforms). The buyer pays a fixed fee plus a share of revenue from jobs sold off the output. Brokers are a secondary channel, using it as sell-side data-room prep.
ideas.problem: Acquired trades firms often run on paper, desk phones and old PCs, so the owner cannot see permit errors, warranty problems or job margins. Any AI, field-service software or roll-up integration needs structured data first. Meanwhile decades of installs sit in file drawers as an unused equipment-age database.
ideas.solution: A two-person crew with document scanners and phone capture spends 5-10 days on site. Vision-model extraction pulls customer, address, equipment make/model/serial, install date, service history, warranty status and membership status. Output is import-ready for ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro and QuickBooks, plus an 'asset-age' list: homes with systems older than a set threshold, expiring warranties, lapsed maintenance customers and contract renewals. It includes a letter/SMS campaign and prepaid-membership offer templates, with job tagging so results are measured.
ideas.why_now: Handwriting and form extraction from photos became accurate and cheap in 2025-2026. Bain's 2026 GP outlook says 39% of GPs expect no material financial impact from AI on portfolio companies this year, and Bain's midyear report says leaders redesign workflows rather than layering tools on top. Both point to data readiness as the gap. First-time buyers of small trades firms are more numerous than ever, and each faces the same digitization backlog.
ideas.revenue_model: $8-15K fixed fee per business, plus 8-10% of first-year revenue from jobs tagged to campaigns generated from the output. Sell-side version for brokers: $3-5K data-room prep before listing.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: What looks like clutter is a proprietary, geocoded equipment-age database of thousands of households, the highest-intent lead list in the trades, and the buyer paid for it in the purchase price without knowing. Rob Brooks found '30,000 customer records' in filing cabinets, 13-year-old computers and desk phones, could not see permit or warranty problems until he digitized, and reached $1.3M EBITDA from $340K SDE in 14 months with about 800 customers prepaying three years of membership (https://www.acquiringminds.co/articles/rob-brooks-gary-air).
